2027-01-13.title: Second Wednesday of Denha
2027-01-13.readTitle: Readings of the day (First Set; mapped from the official calendar, verify locally)
readings: He is our peace; in his flesh he has made both groups into one
Do you love me? Feed my sheep
2027-01-13.verse: For he is our peace; in his flesh he has made both groups into one and has broken down the dividing wall, that is, the hostility between us.
theo: Paul asks the Gentile Christians of Ephesus to remember where they came from: “without Christ, being aliens from the commonwealth of Israel, and strangers to the covenants of promise, having no hope and without God in the world.” That was the condition of our own ancestors before the Gospel reached these shores. “But now in Christ Jesus you who once were far off have been brought near by the blood of Christ. For he is our peace; in his flesh he has made both groups into one and has broken down the dividing wall.” In the Temple of Jerusalem a stone barrier kept Gentiles out of the inner courts. On the Cross Christ tore down every such wall, in order to “create in himself one new humanity in place of the two”. And so Paul concludes: “you are no longer strangers and aliens, but you are citizens with the saints and also members of the household of God”.

Who will care for this one household? In the Gospel the risen Lord, by the lake, asks Simon Peter three times: “Simon son of John, do you love me?” Only after each answer of love does he give the charge: feed my lambs, tend my sheep, feed my sheep. The flock never becomes Peter's property; Jesus still calls them my sheep. And the first qualification for caring for them is not talent or position but love for Christ. This touches each of us: parents who feed their children in the faith, teachers and catechists, priests and bishops, and the Successor of Peter. Then Jesus adds the hardest word: “Follow me.” Love for the Shepherd leads to laying down one's life for the sheep, as Peter himself would do in Rome.
outline: Ask: have you ever felt like an outsider? What made you feel at home?
The dividing wall broken down on the Cross.
Love for Christ before service of the flock.
live: Greet and welcome someone new or alone at church this Sunday.
Before each service you give this week, at home or in the parish, say quietly: Lord, you know that I love you.
2027-01-13.prayer: Lord Jesus, you are our peace. By your blood you brought near those who were far off and broke down the walls that divide us. Make me a member of your household who welcomes others, and give me a love for you that shows itself in caring for your sheep. Amen.
altar: At the altar the near and the far, rich and poor, people of every language are reconciled to God in one body through the Cross. The Holy Qurbana is offered in communion with the Pope and our bishops, the shepherds to whom Christ has entrusted his sheep.

quick: Once far off, we have been brought near by the blood of Christ.
Christ is our peace; he has broken down the dividing wall.
Love for Christ comes before caring for his flock.
2027-01-13.action: Welcome someone new or alone at church this week.
2027-01-13.question: Whom do I still keep on the other side of a wall?

family.explain: St Paul says that in Jesus nobody is a stranger: we are all members of God's family.
family.intention: We pray for people who feel lonely or left out.
family.ask: Ask: “Whom can we welcome into our home or our circle this week?”

illus: A family from Bihar moved to a small town in Thrissur district for work. At their first Sunday Qurbana they stood at the back, unsure of the language. An elderly woman walked over, took the children by the hand and seated them beside her grandchildren. Years later the father said: that day we stopped being migrants and became parishioners.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, you are our peace. Break down every wall among us and make us one household as we gather. Amen.
share: You who once were far off have been brought near (Ephesians 2:13). How has God brought me near?
He has broken down the dividing wall (Ephesians 2:14). What walls remain in my heart?
Do you love me? Feed my sheep (John 21:17). Whom has the Lord entrusted to my care?
interc: For the Pope, our Major Archbishop and all pastors, that they may feed Christ's flock with love.
For migrants and strangers, that they may find a home in the Church.
For communities divided by caste, language or region.
For parents and catechists who feed the young in faith.
For our group, that we may welcome others as we have been welcomed.
pm.close: Father, through the Cross of your Son you have made us one household. Keep us in his peace and make us faithful in caring for his sheep. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

homily: Dear friends, St Paul asks us to remember: once we were far off, strangers to the covenants of promise, having no hope and without God in the world (Ephesians 2:12). According to our tradition, our ancestors in Kerala received the Gospel from the apostle Thomas. Christ came looking for us.

But now, says Paul, you who once were far off have been brought near by the blood of Christ. For he is our peace; he has broken down the dividing wall (Ephesians 2:13–14). In Christ no one is a foreigner. We are citizens with the saints and members of the household of God (Ephesians 2:19).
Who cares for this household? The risen Jesus asks Peter three times: do you love me? And each time he adds: feed my sheep (John 21:15–17). Before he gives Peter a task, he asks for his love.
Each of us has sheep to feed: our children, our students, the sick, the new family in the parish. Let us serve them out of love for Christ, and break down the walls that still divide us. Amen.
kids: Children, Jesus asked Peter: do you love me? Then take care of my sheep. You can take care of Jesus' sheep too: be a friend to the new child in your class!

intro: Christ gathers the far and the near into one household and entrusts it to shepherds who love him.

q: Peace, peace, to the far and the near, says the LORD; and I will heal them.
But now in Christ Jesus you who once were far off have been brought near by the blood of Christ.
points.apply: Thank God this week for the gift of faith that reached our land.

q: For a child has been born for us, a son given to us; authority rests upon his shoulders; and he is named Wonderful Counselor, Mighty God, Everlasting Father, Prince of Peace.
For he is our peace; in his flesh he has made both groups into one and has broken down the dividing wall, that is, the hostility between us.
points.apply: Take down one wall: speak to someone you have kept at a distance.

q: I myself will be the shepherd of my sheep, and I will make them lie down, says the Lord GOD.
A second time he said to him, “Simon son of John, do you love me?” He said to him, “Yes, Lord; you know that I love you.” Jesus said to him, “Tend my sheep.”
points.apply: Pray daily for the Pope, our Major Archbishop and your parish priest.

concl: In Christ no one is a stranger.
Love for the Shepherd becomes care for the flock.
2027-01-13.resolve: This week welcome one newcomer, and pray every day for our shepherds.
